articles.title: Up 85% YTD! Circuit-to-circuit penny stock under ₹2 hits 5% upper circuit for the third straight session; do you own?
articles.source: mint - markets
articles.summary: An unnamed FMCG penny stock priced under ₹2 has hit a 5% upper circuit for three consecutive sessions, marking an 85% gain year-to-date.
articles.explain: An 'upper circuit' is a regulatory limit on how high a stock price can rise during a single trading session to prevent excessive speculation. When a stock hits this limit, trading is essentially frozen because there are only buyers and no sellers. Penny stocks are considered highly speculative and risky for average investors due to the potential for total loss of capital.

related.title: Penny stock under ₹10 hits 5% upper circuit on Dhanteras 2026 date; finds no seller for third straight session

story.title: Penny Stock Market Rally
story.so_far: Penny stocks are shares of small companies that trade at very low prices. Because they are often illiquid and have low market capitalizations, they are highly volatile and prone to sudden, sharp price movements known as 'upper circuits' or 'lower circuits'—limits set by exchanges to prevent extreme price swings in a single day.

story.title: Combating Illicit Stablecoin Activity
